text: Testing plays a key role in modern software development. Developers write unit tests to check small parts of code, such as individual functions. Integration tests then make sure these parts work together correctly. Many teams also use test-driven development, where tests are written before the actual code. This approach helps programmers think clearly about what the code should do. Although writing tests takes time, it brings real benefits. Good tests give developers confidence to change code without breaking existing features. As a result, teams can release software faster and with fewer bugs, which keeps users happy and reduces long-term costs.
